From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
pipoca
Wikipedia pt

Etymology 1

[edit]

Unknown. Sources are unanimous in mentioning a borrowing from Old Tupi pipoka,[1][2][3][4] from pira (“skin”) +‎ pok (“to crack”) +‎ -a,[5][6] but the word is unattested and there's no evidence of Tupian peoples making popcorn.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /piˈpɔ.kɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /piˈpɔ.kɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /piˈpɔ.ka/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /piˈpɔ.kɐ/

  • Rhymes: -ɔkɐ
  • Hyphenation: pi‧po‧ca

Noun

[edit]

pipoca f (plural pipocas, diminutive pipoquinha)

  1. popcorn
    • 1865, Bernardo Guimarães, “A orgia dos duendes”, in Poesias diversas, Rio de Janeiro: B. L. Garnier, page 269:
      Junto d’elle um vermelho diabo / Que sahíra do antro das phócas, / Pendurado n’um páo pelo rabo, / No borralho torrava pipócas.
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
    • 1875, José de Alencar, O Sertanejo, volume 2, Rio de Janeiro: B. L. Garnier, page 175:
      […] só tinha que não podia ver cabeção de cacondê que não ficasse logo como pipoca na frigideira!
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
  2. small skin boil
    Synonyms: see Thesaurus:pústula
  3. tapeworm cyst embedded in meat
    Synonyms: canjica, canjiquinha, cisticerco, cisto, pipoquinha
  4. (Brazil, colloquial, pathology) avian pox (disease caused by Avipoxvirus)
    Synonyms: bouba aviária, caroço
  5. (Brazil) candelabra tree (Senna didymobotrya)

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Portuguese pipoca (“popcorn”).

Noun

[edit]

pipoca f (plural pipocas)

  1. (Bolivia) popcorn
    Synonyms: see Thesaurus:palomita

Further reading

[edit]
